title: Choose a mutable String alternative
answer: Use `StringBuilder` for mutable text in ordinary single-threaded or thread-confined code. It lets you append, insert, replace, delete, and reverse characters without creating a new immutable String for every change. Use `StringBuffer` only when you specifically need its synchronized mutable operations for a shared buffer. The final result can be converted back to an immutable String with `toString()`. For most modern application code, `StringBuilder` is the default mutable alternative to String.
